scenes.title: Autopilot Agents: decide the operating model before the rollout
scenes.body: Bottom line: treat Copilot Autopilot as a bounded standing role, not a better chatbot. Approve one private-preview pilot only where a named leader owns the goal, access boundary, cost and outcomes.
scenes.narration: Bottom line: treat Copilot Autopilot as a bounded standing role, not a better chatbot. Approve one private-preview pilot only where a named leader owns the goal, access boundary, cost and outcomes.
claims: Copilot Autopilot, previously called Scout, was announced as a persistent digital teammate with its own identity, memory, computer and workspace; people set its objective and boundaries and remain informed and in control.
Microsoft said Copilot Autopilot was expanding to private preview at the end of September 2026; the announcement does not establish general availability.
As an architectural lens, Microsoft Foundry defines an autopilot by a persistent standing role and its own identity, security profile and accountable manager, not by a changing feature list.
In the Foundry model, autonomy remains bounded: the organization controls when an autopilot responds, who it interacts with, what it accesses and which actions it can take.
The Foundry blueprint model separates reusable agent logic and infrastructure from team-specific business access, with each created instance receiving its own identity, permissions and assignment.
